messages:
sara (support): Hey team — inbound from ACME: massive 503/500 spike on hosted inference for /v1/generate since ~10:05 UTC. They report ~30% of requests now returning 503 with `upstream error: worker exited` and a few 500s. sample request-id: req_9a3f. Customer is seeing timeouts in prod. Escalating, can oncall triage?

mike (oncall): I'm on it. Can you paste a few full request ids and which model they hit?

sara (support): Request ids: req_9a3f, req_9a7b, req_9b20. Hitting `redwood-chat-8b-v1` (hosted), routed to us-east-1. They said payloads include long context (~14k tokens) + streaming.

mike (oncall): Checking worker pool states... `kubectl get pods -n inference --selector=svc=hosted-us-east-1 -o wide` shows many pods in CrashLoopBackOff. Looking at pod logs for one: `inference-worker-7f9d8` logs show repeated `SIGSEGV` followed by `OOM killer` entries.

aj (eng-runtime): paste of recent log snippet from pod: ```
[2026-03-15T10:06:12Z] runtime: kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (inference-worker) total-vm:...
[2026-03-15T10:06:12Z] runtime: cuda runtime error: out of memory
[2026-03-15T10:06:12Z] inference-worker: terminating with signal SIGSEGV (core dumped)
```

lina (eng-ml): That pattern looks like a GPU OOM followed by an inconsistent state leading to segfault on cleanup path. Any recent model variant or runtime deploys?

aj (eng-runtime): We had a canary rollout at 03:42 UTC that switched kernel selection logic for attention kernels and adjusted KV cache eviction heuristics (deploy id: deploy/2026-03-15/blue-2247, commit `ab3f9d2`). Noticed a spike in memory usage in canary metrics but not flagged.

mike (oncall): Can we repro locally with a stress script? If it's KV growth + long context + streaming it might be hitting per-request GPU memory worst-case.

aj (eng-runtime): Repro steps I'm trying now: `python tools/repro_run.py --model redwood-chat-8b-v1 --context-file long_prompt_14k.json --batch 12 --concurrency 16 --stream` (we also have a `hey` para: `hey -n 1000 -c 40 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`). Initial run on a dev rig hits OOM at ~10 concurrent streams.

ops-bot: :warning: 5 pods in inference-hosted-us-east-1 are restarting every ~30s (container restartCount > 5).

aj (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation options: 1) Rollback kernel selection change (deploy rollback to `ab3f9d2` previous commit `7c1d0a9`) 2) Force-route heavy customers to fallback model variant with smaller KV (e.g., `redwood-chat-8b-v1-compact`) 3) Temporarily disable streaming for high-context requests (reduces concurrent KV growth) 4) Increase pod GPU memory reservation / reduce batch concurrency.

mike (oncall): Immediate action: route ACME to fallback variant + scale up of dedicated fallback pool. Also I'll drain the crashing pods and trigger a rollback if we see same behavior in non-canary. Any objections? :thinking: 

lina (eng-ml): Good call routing customers. We should also add an input-size guard at the routing layer to reject >12k token payloads with a 4xx and guidance. That's a longer term fix but reduces blast radius.

deploy-bot: Deploy request created: `rollback deploy/2026-03-15/blue-2247 -> deploy/2026-03-10/green-1981` by mike (oncall). ETA ~6m.

aj (eng-runtime): I'll start a local reproducer with exact request ids and payloads from ACME. If we can reproduce deterministically I'll open a runtime bug with `SIGSEGV` stack trace. Please collect any core dumps (`/var/crash`) and `nvidia-smi -q` outputs.

sara (support): FYI ACME confirms they've been routed to fallback and 503s dropped to ~2% within last 10m. They're asking for root cause and timeline for full fix.

mike (oncall): Rolling back now. Observability: memory headroom graphs show rollback target has lower peak mem. After rollback, pod restarts stopped. I'll keep monitoring for 30m.

aj (eng-runtime): After reproducer, stack trace shows `libattention.so` in `attention_forward` then `free_kv_cache` -> SIGSEGV during cleanup when GPU OOM occurred mid-forward. Suspect a race between OOM path and kernel resource cleanup. Filing bug: https://tracker.internal/RI-4621 with stack, repro, and CC: eng-runtime, eng-ml.

lina (eng-ml): I'll prepare model-side mitigations: lower kv_cache_max by default for streaming, and add guardrails for extremely long contexts + fallback modes.

mike (oncall): Incident summary for customer and SRE postmortem: root cause = regression in kernel selection/kv eviction heuristics introduced in `deploy/blue-2247` causing unbounded per-request GPU memory during high-concurrency, long-context streaming; led to GPU OOMs followed by segfaults on cleanup and container crash loops. Mitigation = rollback + route affected customers to compact variant + added temporary input size guard. Next steps = engineering bug (RI-4621), model guardrails, improved canary mem alerts. I'll create the incident ticket and link to customer update.

sara (support): Thanks — sending customer update now. :heavy_check_mark:
